themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the system often changes while you measure it, so the models begin by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: Today's answers on cross-channel incrementality all warn that the platform changes the treatment while you measure it, echoing answer engine optimization (no stable baseline), identity resolution (no truth about who is who), content governance (reviewers disagree) and B2B buying-group signal (few accounts ever buy).

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people holding the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: Agentic traffic answers build a fast lane so declaring beats spoofing, journey orchestration answers admit channel owners are paid to keep sending, the semantic context layer is called a political fight rather than a data problem, and incrementality answers note platforms have no reason to expose how delivery works.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: Generative content governance answers converge on an approved-claims registry because implied claims resist automation, and the semantic context layer answers conclude that conflicting definitions of 'active customer' are legitimate and must be disclosed rather than resolved.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and guess whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: Downstream consent and deletion answers agree that black-box partners and trained models cannot show person-level proof, identity resolution answers say platform owners profit from keeping walls up, and ad supply integrity answers say the parties measuring fake traffic profit from it.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: All three models answer safe agent execution with a proxy or gateway enforcing spend and audience caps, consent enforcement answers route every data exit through a single checkpoint, and journey orchestration answers propose one shared contact log with veto power.
